comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Terms and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has $3 billion available under a revolving credit agreement expiring on April 29, 2027, with no outstanding borrowings as of December 28, 2024, and interest rates tied to SOFR or Base Rate plus margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose that their respective Revolving Credit Facilities had no outstanding borrowings as of their 2024 fiscal year-end (MU as of August 29, 2024; AMD as of December 28, 2024). Additionally, both companies use SOFR as a benchmark for interest rates on borrowings under these facilities, though AMD also offers a Base Rate option and specifies different margin structures (0.575% to 1.20% for SOFR vs MU's 1.00% to 1.75% plus credit spread adjustment).

sentences.text: Under the Revolving Credit Facility, borrowings would generally bear interest at a rate equal to adjusted term SOFR plus 1.00% to 1.75%, depending on our corporate credit ratings.

Adjusted term SOFR for the Revolving Credit Facility agreement is the SOFR benchmark plus a credit spread adjustment ranging from approximately 0.11% to 0.43% depending on the applicable interest period selected.
The Company has $3 billion available under a revolving credit agreement, as amended, that expires on April 29, 2027 (Revolving Credit Agreement).
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had no outstanding borrowings under the Revolving Credit Agreement.
Each SOFR Loan will bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the applicable SOFR plus a margin between 0.575% and 1.20%.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom entered into a five-year, $7.5 billion unsecured revolving credit agreement in January 2021, which includes a $500 million letter of credit facility and allows borrowing and repayment until January 19, 2026. The company had no outstanding borrowings under this facility at the end of both 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to MU, Broadcom (AVGO) had no borrowings outstanding under its revolving credit facility at the end of fiscal 2024 (November 3, 2024). Both MU and AVGO utilize unsecured revolving credit facilities to manage liquidity. However, the disclosures differ in that AVGO's summary focuses on the facility size ($7.5 billion) and letter of credit availability, while MU's detailed item 8 text provided focuses on the specific interest rate mechanics (SOFR margins and credit spread adjustments).

comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Limits and Maturities
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company expanded its 5-year $5.0 billion and 364-day $5.0 billion revolving credit facilities to $7.0 billion and $8.0 billion respectively, with maturity dates extended to February 2029 and January 2025. These facilities are unsecured general obligations and had no borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Like MU and AMD, Intel (INTC) reported no borrowings outstanding under its revolving credit facilities as of the end of fiscal 2024 (December 28, 2024). A key similarity is the unsecured nature of the debt. A significant difference is that INTC's disclosure highlights a recent expansion of facility limits (from $5.0B to $7.0B/$8.0B) and maturity extensions in 2024, whereas MU's provided text focuses on the interest rate calculation methodology rather than facility term changes.

sentences.text: Under the Revolving Credit Facility, borrowings would generally bear interest at a rate equal to adjusted term SOFR plus 1.00% to 1.75%, depending on our corporate credit ratings.
